A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and formatting changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, retrieval and latent-space experiments, including loss comparisons and unseen-architecture evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative Objaverse retrieval and NeRF captioning/Q&A results.

M1.justification: The graph conversions, GMN encoder, decoder and representation-learning losses remain unchanged. Section 4.4 adds a downstream adaptation that replaces LLaNA's nf2vec encoder with the GMN encoder to condition a Llama 2 language model for captioning and Q&A.

E1.justification: v3 adds brief captioning, detailed captioning and single-round Q&A with ShapeNeRF–Text training. It also adds within-Objaverse instance retrieval using MLP, tri-planar and hash-based representations. Objaverse was already used for qualitative queries in v2; ObjaNeRF becoming MLP^OB is a rename.

E2.justification: v3 adds RANDOM ranking to the retained retrieval comparisons and evaluates LLaNA in the new single-architecture language experiments. Existing nf2vec and Cardace classification comparisons remain unchanged. LLaNA's dashed multi-architecture rows do not represent evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce retrieval over 1,884 Objaverse objects and language evaluation with ALL versus MLP training, S-BERT/SimCSE metrics and additional n-gram metrics. Existing classification settings and training budgets remain unchanged. The single-architecture language objective is ambiguous: Tables 11–13 say LR+C although the text says this setting drops contrastive loss.

E4.justification: v3 adds systematic quantitative distribution-shift testing: encoders trained on ShapenetRender retrieve matching Objaverse instances across architectures, comparing LR, LC and LR+C in Tables 7 and 18. v2 provided only qualitative Objaverse evidence. Existing qualitative cases, latent-space analyses and architecture/loss comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added analytical RANDOM baseline is a comparator, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Classification values are unchanged, and shared retrieval scores receive finer precision. v3 adds substantial Objaverse and language results: Table 7 reports MLP^OB-to-TRI^OB recall@1 of 9.82% for LR+C versus 2.60% for LR; Tables 12/23 report detailed-captioning S-BERT scores of 74.1 versus LLaNA's 77.4. These are new comparisons, not improvements over v2 under identical settings. ALL/ALL retrieval results remain in Table 17.

T1.justification: The loss definitions in Equations 1–4 and Appendix A's graph-size reasoning are unchanged. v3's Equation 5 spells out the standard chance-recall calculation for RANDOM without introducing substantive new theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The central diverse-architecture, contrastive-learning and hash-table novelty claims remain. The abstract and introduction extend applicability to language tasks, explicitly highlight unseen-data generalization and dataset release, and soften 'superior/exceeding' to 'comparable or superior/matching or exceeding.'

C2.justification: v3 interprets the Objaverse performance drop in terms of distribution shift and the language results as evidence of architecture-agnostic semantic utility. Appendix F explains its preference for semantic text metrics over n-gram metrics. Existing loss-tradeoff explanations and failure cases remain; the ALL/ALL failure discussion moves to Appendix C.

D1.justification: Appendices B/D specify the Objaverse test-set construction from the PointLLM and GPT4Point splits and NerfAcc generation of the new tri-planar/hash NeRFs. The promised release expands from code to code and datasets, still conditional on acceptance. Existing architectural hyperparameters, hardware and training times remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Llama 2, language-evaluation metrics and Objaverse test-split sources, and develops its relationship to LLaNA through the encoder replacement. LLaNA was already cited in v2. The main positioning relative to GMNs, nf2vec and Cardace remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most core prose and section order are preserved with copyediting. Section 4.3 is revised, Section 4.4 and Appendices F/G are added, ObjaNeRF is renamed MLP^OB, and the author order changes. These are localized narrative extensions rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds an LLM branch to Figure 1, introduces Objaverse and language-result tables, and substantially reorganizes table layouts. Figure 4 retains only the cross-dataset examples, with the other examples still available in the appendices. Title/header styling and figure placement change throughout; the underlying t-SNE and appendix retrieval images remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The quantitative Objaverse evaluation strengthens transfer evidence previously supported only by illustrative queries, while captioning/Q&A comparisons test additional usefulness and retain the earlier evidence. The net gain is limited by incomplete language-training documentation, the MLP-only LR+C inconsistency, and the lightly qualified 'comparable' interpretation despite detailed-captioning deficits in Tables 12/23.
